{{short description|American applied mathematician}}
'''Heidi Krista Thornquist''' is an American [[applied mathematics|applied mathematician]] at [[Sandia National Laboratories]] known for her work on the [[Trilinos]] system of software for [[scientific computing]]. Her research interests include [[numerical linear algebra]] and [[electronic circuit simulation]].

Thornquist majored in mathematics at [[Humboldt State University]], graduating ''[[Latin honors|summa cum laude]]'' in 1998.{{r|cv}} She became a doctoral student of Danny C. Sorensen in computational and applied mathematics at [[Rice University]], where she completed her Ph.D. in 2006. Her dissertation was ''Fixed-Polynomial Approximate Spectral Transformations for Preconditioning the Eigenvalue Problem''.{{r|cv|mg}} She began working at Sandia in 2003, while she was still at Rice, and remained there after completing her doctorate.{{r|cv}}

Thornquist is the lead developer of three packages within the Trilinos system: Anasazi, for computing [[eigenvalue]]s, Belos, for solving [[System of linear equations|systems of linear equations]], and Teuchos, a suite of utilities and wrappers.{{r|anasazi}}
